synoptic.summary: High pressure over the southwestern US keeps the area dry and clear: no precipitation or thunder in any launch forecast through Wednesday. Monday a light flow from 165°–210° at 6–10 kt sits 2,000–3,700 ft above the landings, and the launch forecasts hold 120°–160° at the Point all day — no afternoon switch to 320°–360°, although the Salt Lake airport forecast still has 340° from 11:00. Be skeptical: Sunday's launch forecasts also showed no switch, yet by 14:15 Sunday every valley station read 310°–340° at 5–11 kt. A dry shortwave trough passes Tuesday: flow aloft turns to 300°–360°, 23–28 kt about 9,600 ft above landing but only 4–13 kt below 5,700 ft, and mixing deepens to ~3,000 ft. High pressure returns Wednesday with very light flow aloft.
synoptic.afd_excerpt: Otherwise, expect dry conditions and another couple of degrees of warming heading into tomorrow as high pressure builds. A dry shortwave trough will swing through the region on Tuesday, producing slightly cooler temperatures on the order of a few degrees.

pressure.significance: Salt Lake airport sea-level pressure was 1022.4 mb at 16:54 Sunday, down from 1026.1 mb 24 h earlier (and 1025.6 mb at the same time Saturday). A slow fall ahead of Tuesday's dry shortwave, but still high pressure and a light gradient — the local daily wind cycle should dominate, with Tuesday the least settled day.

observations.summary: Readings from 16:15–16:55 Sunday are current (under an hour old at report time), but they describe Sunday evening, not Monday morning. All reporting valley stations show the afternoon flow from 310°–15° at 5–10 kt, with gusts to 19 kt at Spanish Fork and 17 kt at Alpine — the diurnal switch happened Sunday even though the launch forecasts had none. The Point of the Mountain and Draper stations returned no observations.
